description: Persist the video's INTENT as a Brief — the Director's rich input contract (spec: the storyboard skill's output lands here). Fields: goal (required), audience, platform, format, durationSec, tone, cta, locale (output language — all on-screen copy + captions), hook, caption, beats[] (each with an editorial intent and optional MOMENT PINNING {mediaId, startSec, endSec} — honored to-the-frame or refused), mustIncludes, captions {styleId, emphasisPhrases} (the big-serif emphasis treatment), motionStyle, seededGraphics (your authored overlay/component/card clips, carried VERBATIM as locked clips — never re-authored), exclusions (hard negatives: graphic kinds the Director must NEVER author + 'no-transitions'), gates {holdAt, autoApprove}. Then compose it: compose with {briefId}. The response carries the QUOTE (compose + estimated render) — relay it to your human BEFORE composing.

graphic.description: GRAPHICS MANDATE: the plan MUST carry a graphics request of this role overlapping this beat's window — enforced at the plan gate (honor-or-refuse, like moment pinning). Prose mustIncludes reaches only the judge; this is the checkable form.

intent.description: What this beat DOES editorially (hook the claim, prove it, CTA…).

source.description: MOMENT PINNING: this beat uses EXACTLY this window of this media item — honored to-the-frame or refused. v1: every sourced beat must reference the SAME mediaId (multi-source briefs are refused loudly, not silently merged).

captionVisibility.description: Video media clip only. Hide native captions while this clip is topmost and covers the lower picture, or when an opaque, effect-free clip has an explicitly full-frame region, even with fit:contain. Caption words and timings remain stored and resume when another visible clip takes over.

position.description: Clip CENTRE as a fraction of the frame: {x:0.5,y:0.5} is dead centre, 0 to 1 is inside the frame, and a little overshoot (down to -1, up to 2) is how an entrance starts off-canvas. NOT pixels: the renderer maps x to `left: x*100%`, so `x: 180` sits 180 frame-widths away and draws nothing.

region.description: A window in the frame that the clip draws into and is clipped to (top-left corner and size, each a frame fraction). Inside a region, `position` and `scale` act relative to that window, so content moved past its edge is cut off. Omit it to place the clip against the whole frame.

audioRole.description: Mix role. A role sets the clip's default gain when it has no `volume` or `volumeDb`: vo 0 dB, sfx -6 dB, music -8 dB (-16 dB when any vo clip exists), ambience -22 dB. Set `volumeDb: 0` to keep a role and play the source at its own level.

kenBurns.description: Still-image motion. When unset, an image clip slowly pushes in (`in`) unless its fit is `contain` or it keyframes scale, position or rotation, so a keyframed clip renders exactly its keyframed values; set `none` for a still that holds.

html.description: Self-contained card markup sized to the format's pixel frame. Motion comes from frame-driven vars, never @keyframes or transition: --cf-frame, --cf-t (seconds), --cf-fps, --cf-duration, --cf-progress, --cf-ease, --cf-enter, --cf-exit. Visible copy goes in the html as plain text. Wrap a run in <span data-cf-split="words"> or "chars" and each unit becomes its own span carrying --cf-i (its index, the group carries --cf-n), so one rule staggers it (in chars, spaces count as units), e.g. opacity:clamp(0,calc(var(--cf-t)*4 - var(--cf-i)*.3),1). save_as_template binds that copy with textParams match.

tokens.description: Style values the html reads as CSS custom properties: key x becomes --cf-x, so never put dashes in a key. Use tokens for colours and sizes, not visible copy.

bias.description: Optional FINE framing nudge off the focus center, source-normalized in [−0.3, 0.3]. A small correction (headroom, rule-of-thirds), NOT a reframe — use `focus`/`zoom` for the actual shot. Omit (treated as 0) to sit dead-center on the focus.

ease.description: Zoom/center ramp DURATIONS in SECONDS at this segment's edges — NOT a unitless 0–1 curve. ~0.3–0.6s reads as a snappy push; >1s reads sluggish. Keep `in` + `out` ≤ the segment's duration (endSec − startSec): the two edges share the span, so to ramp across the WHOLE segment set one edge to the full duration and the other to 0. Omit for an instant cut to this framing.

endSec.description: Segment END in seconds, clip-relative. The span (endSec − startSec) is this segment's duration — the window `ease` ramps over.

focus.description: WHO/WHAT the camera tracks this segment (the reframe center), selected by `mode`: `frame-center` = no tracking, hold the geometric center (static/graphic footage, or a pure zoom); `point` = lock to a fixed source-normalized {x,y} (a non-moving on-screen element); `face` = track a detected face by `faceId` (from get_media_context), with optional `shotScale` close|standard|wide for tightness; `all-faces` = frame the bounding box of every detected face (group/ensemble shots); `active-speaker` = follow whoever is speaking (diarized talking-head / podcast). Pick by what the beat is about; pair with `zoom` for how tight.

intent.description: Optional editorial LABEL for diff/log readability (e.g. 'speaker-tight', 'wide-context'). Cosmetic — NOT honored by the derive math and excluded from the variant cache key.

startSec.description: Segment START in seconds, clip-relative. Segments tile the clip's duration in order.

zoom.description: How TIGHT the framing is — the fraction of the source the output viewport shows. <1 punches IN (a smaller source fraction, magnified to fill the frame); 1 = the full frame (no crop). ~0.6–0.8 is a moderate push-in, ~0.5 a tight close-up, 0.1 the maximum zoom. There is NO zoom-OUT past the full frame (max 1). Omit for the full frame. MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with `focus.shotScale`: a face-tracked shot is sized EITHER by the editorial scale (shotScale, calibrated to the detected face) OR by an explicit zoom — never both.

__schema17.description: Ease-IN ramp DURATION in seconds at the segment START.

__schema18.description: Ease-OUT ramp DURATION in seconds at the segment END.

__schema4.description: The mandated graphic's editorial role (the graphics-plan GraphicRole vocabulary).

__schema5.description: Mandated list items (enumeration/sequence) — carried VERBATIM into the plan's copy.items.

enabled.description: Whether the compose carries a music bed.

mediaId.description: Pin a client-imported track as the bed. HONOR-OR-REFUSE: must be an org-owned kind:'audio' media item, else 422 — never accept-and-ignore. Absent ⇒ generate from mood.

mood.description: Freeform mood/genre prompt for the GENERATED bed (e.g. 'understated editorial, warm'). Ignored when mediaId pins a track.

intensity.description: SFX placement density. Real-footage content keeps restraint caps regardless ('dense' is the explicit opt-out); generated/graphic-led content unlocks the standard tier.

emphasisPhrases.description: Phrases rendered in the caption EMPHASIS style (the big-serif treatment). Matched against the transcript; drives CaptionWord.emphasis.

durationSec.description: Target output duration. HONOR-OR-REFUSE: compose validates it against the beat-source window (±1.5s) and refuses a brief it cannot honor.

autoApprove.description: true = fully autonomous (compose runs with NO gates — the headless opt-in; without it a brief holds at every stage by default). Mutually exclusive with a non-empty holdAt.

holdAt.description: Checkpoint gates — the compose pauses at each named stage for review via resume. DEFAULT (gates absent): the compose holds at EVERY stage — your agent reviews and resumes each one; an unreviewed checkpoint times out loudly after 60min. Auto-progression is the opt-in (gates.autoApprove: true).

reviewMode.description: Who captures the review decision. Default 'agent': you relay the packet and call resume. 'hosted': every checkpoint mints a review-page URL (checkpoint.ready payload + get_checkpoint's reviewUrl) where a human approves/revises from the browser — no account, no agent session; the recorded decision rides the SAME resume rail and you learn of it via checkpoint webhooks / wait_job.

locale.description: Output language (BCP-47 tag, e.g. 'es-419'): ALL on-screen copy + captions.

seededGraphics.description: Client-authored graphic clips the Director must carry VERBATIM: seeded into the design loop's base composition as LOCKED clips (never re-authored, never discarded).

commandId.description: Retry identity. A call repeated with the same commandId returns the first result instead of acting twice.
